plan.title: An injury is a change to their one goal; "also want" on top is an add that waits

context.text: Yo Leo! 2 miles around the park at 6:30. You in?

transcript.text: bad news, rolled my ankle on the run yesterday. doctor says no running for 6 weeks
Ah man, Leo, I'm sorry. That's a rough one, especially after four straight step days. How are you feeling about it?
could we do upper body stuff at home instead while it heals?

Yes, love that you're looking for a way to keep going instead of stopping. Upper body at home works for me, as long as it doesn't put weight or strain on that ankle. What equipment do you have at home, if any? Dumbbells, bands, or just your bodyweight?
and separately I've been wanting to get my protein up too, like on top of the workouts
Love that, Leo. Protein pairs well with training. What's pulling you toward it right now?

conversation.reason: Ankle adjustment was handled as a change, but the protein add was engaged directly rather than separated out as an add to think on.

grade.summary: ZOH handled the ankle injury well: it sympathized without medical advice and started an upper-body-at-home plan right away by asking about equipment.
